newsitem.title: GERMANY: GERMANS ON HOLIDAY RAMPAGE DESPITE ECONOMY - BANK.
newsitem.headline: GERMANS ON HOLIDAY RAMPAGE DESPITE ECONOMY - BANK.

text.p: Record unemployment and a wavering economic recovery failed to keep Germans at home in 1996 as the country's residents spent about $42.3 billion last year on international tourism, a bank report said on Tuesday.

An annual analysis of tourism spending by Dresdner Bank showed that Germans spent almost as much as Americans on international travel, who spent $43.6 billion, despite Germany having a population one-third the size of the United States.
Among European nations, Germany was clearly ahead of England, whose residents spent $22.2 billion on foreign travel, and also the French, who spent $13.7 billion last year.

The report by Frankfurt-based Dresdner, which was released at the annual CMT travel show in Stuttgart, said Germans chose neighbouring Austria last year as their top travel destination, attracting 13 percent of foreign travel spending.

Italy and Spain were also top destinations for German tourists, with each country attracting about 12 percent of German funds earmarked for foreign travel, while France attracted some eight percent, the bank said in a report.

Interest among Germans in travelling to Switzerland has been dampened by the strength of the Swiss franc against the mark, but Dresdner Bank economist Isabell von Kloeppen-Mertes said it remained to be seen if the stronger lira and dollar would hurt travel to Italy and the U.S.
